case-sara.text: [Checks clock, tearful] I know we're nearly done. I still feel sad, though.
case-sara.suggestion: We have a few minutes left, and the sadness is still here. We don't have to make it disappear. What would help you make the transition out of the room?

case-sara.text: [Hesitant] There's something else about my mum, but it's a lot. Maybe this isn't the time.
case-sara.suggestion: It sounds important, and we don't have time to give it enough space today. Shall we note where you want to begin next time and use these last minutes to settle here?

case-sara.text: [Quietly] I don't want to leave pretending I'm okay. I'm not.
case-sara.suggestion: You don't have to pretend. We are ending the hour, not asking you to be okay. Could we pause with how you are now before you go?

case-sara.text: [Sniffs] I have to go straight back to work. I don't want to walk into a meeting like this.
case-sara.suggestion: Let's leave some time for that transition. What would help you feel ready enough for the meeting, without needing to push every feeling away?

case-sara.text: [Looks around] Can I sit for a moment before I leave? I don't want to rush out.
case-sara.suggestion: Yes, let's use the last couple of minutes to sit. We can pause the talking and give you time to notice the room again.

case-sara.text: [Worried] What if all this comes back tonight? I can't call you at ten, can I?
case-sara.suggestion: I can't offer a call at ten. Let's use the time we have to think about what might help tonight and what support you can actually reach.

case-sara.text: [Reflective] I want to remember that wanting company isn't wrong. But I don't need another task this week.
case-sara.suggestion: Then let's leave it as something to remember, not another task. Is ‘wanting company isn't wrong’ the wording you want to take with you today?

case-sara.text: [Softly] I don't know how to sum this up. We've talked about so much.
case-sara.suggestion: There has been a lot. As we finish, is there one moment you want to keep, or would you rather I briefly reflect what I heard and you tell me what fits?

case-sara.text: [Uneasy] I feel a bit exposed after saying all that. I wish I could take some of it back.
case-sara.suggestion: You're feeling exposed now. Before we end, would a quiet moment help, or is there something you need to say about having shared it?

case-sara.text: [Checks phone] My friend is meeting me outside. I think I'd rather just walk with her than talk more today.
case-sara.suggestion: A walk with her sounds like the transition you want. Shall we stop the work here and take a quiet moment before you meet her?

case-sara.text: [Tearful but steady] I'm okay to leave. I just want us to come back to the part about asking for help.
case-sara.suggestion: Let's note that for next time: asking for help. Before we end, is there anything you want to say about how it feels to stop here?

case-sara.text: [Small sigh] I'm not lighter exactly. I'm tired, and I want to go home slowly.
case-sara.suggestion: Tired, rather than lighter. We can let that be where we stop today. What would going home slowly look like for you?

case-arne.text: [Tearful] We’re nearly done. I’m still sad.
case-arne.suggestion: We have a few minutes left. What would help you leave with the sadness still here?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] Can I sit a little before I leave?
case-arne.suggestion: Yes. Let’s use the last minutes to sit, without more questions.

case-arne.text: [Hesitant] There’s something else, but it needs more time.
case-arne.suggestion: Let’s note where you want to begin next time, rather than open it hurriedly now.

case-arne.text: [Steady] I want to return to asking Emma for company next time.
case-arne.suggestion: We’ll note that. Before we finish, what do you need for the transition out of here?

case-arne.text: [Thoughtful] I want to take “I loved her and I was tired” with me.
case-arne.suggestion: Those are your words to keep. Shall we stop there and take a quiet moment?

case-arne.text: [Tired] I don’t want another task this week.
case-arne.suggestion: No new task. We can finish by noticing what you want to remember, or simply pause.

case-arne.text: [Softly] Tom is meeting me outside. A walk would be good.
case-arne.suggestion: That sounds like the transition you want. Shall we leave the work here for today?

case-arne.text: [Unsure] I don’t know how to sum it all up.
case-arne.suggestion: We don’t need a perfect summary. Is there one moment you want to keep before we end?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I’m ready to go, but slowly.
case-arne.suggestion: We can stop here and leave you a moment to get ready at your own pace.

case-arne.text: [Worried] I may feel lonely again tonight.
case-arne.suggestion: That may return. In our last minutes, would it help to consider what support you want tonight?

case-arne.text: [Tearful, steady] I can leave. I don’t need the tears gone first.
case-arne.suggestion: We can end with the tears still here. Let’s take a moment before you stand up.

case-arne.text: [Reflective] I’m glad we talked. I’m also worn out.
case-arne.suggestion: Both matter as we finish. What would help with leaving today, when you’re this tired?

case-arne.text: [Tearful, watchful] I’m okay to leave, but don’t call this resolved.
case-arne.suggestion: It isn’t resolved. We’re ending the hour, and can note what you want to return to.

case-arne.text: [Hesitant] I remembered something else. There are only five minutes, aren’t there?
case-arne.suggestion: Yes. Shall we mark where to begin next time, rather than rush into it today?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I want company tonight, but I don’t want you making calls for me.
case-arne.suggestion: You decide what contact you want. We can use the last minutes to clarify it, without my taking over.

case-arne.text: [Tired] I understand more, but I don’t feel lighter.
case-arne.suggestion: We can end with understanding and tiredness, without requiring relief. What would help the transition home?

case-arne.text: [Uncertain] Those words fit here. I don’t want to promise I’ll use them at home.
case-arne.suggestion: No promise needed. Is there anything you want to carry, or would you prefer a quiet ending?

case-arne.text: [Tearful] It feels strange to go from this straight onto the bus.
case-arne.suggestion: Let’s leave a few minutes for the change of pace. What would make that journey manageable?

case-arne.text: [Careful] We opened a lot. Can we just name where we’re leaving it?
case-arne.suggestion: Yes. What feels most unfinished to you? We can note it without opening it further.

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I’d rather walk alone after this. That doesn’t mean I’m shutting everyone out.
case-arne.suggestion: A quiet walk is your choice for this transition. We don’t have to interpret it as withdrawal.

case-arne.text: [Hesitant] Could you remind me what you heard, without a big conclusion?
case-arne.suggestion: Briefly: you loved Eva, the care exhausted you, and you want room for both. What fits, or needs changing?

case-arne.text: [Worried] If tonight is rough, I can’t call you whenever I like.
case-arne.suggestion: That’s right. Within the time left, shall we consider support you can actually reach tonight?

case-arne.text: [Softly] I’m ready to leave, and I wish I could stay.
case-arne.suggestion: Both can be here as we end. Let’s take a moment before you stand up.

case-arne.text: [Steady] No more questions today, please. Just a minute before I go.
case-arne.suggestion: A minute without questions. We can pause here and finish gently.

case-arne.text: [Firmly] We can end the hour. Don’t tell me I’m leaving in a better place.
case-arne.suggestion: We can end without that claim. What do you need for the transition as you actually are?

case-arne.text: [Tearful, alert] I’m okay to go, but not to answer another deep question first.
case-arne.suggestion: No deeper question. We can leave a quiet moment before you go.

case-arne.text: [Watchful] There’s unfinished anger. Please don’t make a neat summary of it.
case-arne.suggestion: We can note “unfinished anger” without tidying it. Is that enough of a marker for next time?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I’m embarrassed about what I said. Don’t reassure me with “it was brave.”
case-arne.suggestion: I won’t use that label. Would a quiet pause help before leaving, or something simple you want me to hear?

case-arne.text: [Firmly] I need us to stop on time. Talking more isn’t always kinder.
case-arne.suggestion: You’re right to name the time. We’ll stop the work now and use the remaining moment for the transition.

case-arne.text: [Hesitant] I brought something important up late. I don’t want to squeeze it into two minutes.
case-arne.suggestion: We won’t squeeze it in. What brief marker would help us return to it next time?

case-arne.text: [Watchful] Don’t plan my evening for me. I have one practical question before I go.
case-arne.suggestion: Your evening is yours. What is the practical question we can address in the time left?

case-arne.text: [Tearful] I want quiet, but I don’t want to feel dismissed.
case-arne.suggestion: We can pause together, then mark clearly when we’re finishing. You won’t need to guess from my silence.

case-arne.text: [Tired] I found words for it here. I’m not sure I’ll have them when I get home.
case-arne.suggestion: You don’t have to carry all of this home today. Would you like to keep one phrase, or finish with a quiet moment?

case-arne.text: [Quietly] I’d like to return to the relief next time. Not the hospital details.
case-arne.suggestion: We’ll note the relief, without hospital details. Is there anything simple you need before we finish?

case-arne.text: [Careful] If tonight is hard, I need real options, not “call whenever.”
case-arne.suggestion: I can’t offer open-ended calls. In the time left, let’s clarify support you can actually reach and want to use.

case-arne.text: [Steady] I’m leaving sad. I also feel heard. Let both be true.
case-arne.suggestion: Both can be true. We can stop here, without asking the sadness to become something else.
